about: AgentNet builder bench: each task is a merged commit; the runner checks out fix_sha with files_allowed reverted to fix_sha^ and asks the builder loop to make failing_tests pass. Judge: scripts/bench/score.py. Never edit together with the harness it scores. split=dev: visible to the Society; the holdout tasks live in holdout.json (never in any model context; only the controller reads their scores).

tasks.task: The maintenance activity tool loop gives the model no sight of its turn budget, so live tries spent every turn on reads and never answered. Every tool result must state how many turns are left after it; before the last allowed turn the loop must send a final-turn directive telling the model to submit now with what it has; and a tool call made on the final turn must fail the try with error class turn_budget without being executed.

The Railway release adapter does not match Railway's live GraphQL schema: deploymentRollback(id) returns a Boolean and serviceInstanceDeployV2 returns the new deployment id as a String, so no selection set is valid on either. Discovery must accept these shapes. Rollback must first read the target deployment and refuse one from another environment or with canRollback=false, send the bare mutation, and resolve the new deployment from the deployment list; a rollback not yet listed is tracked by a pending handle that reads as DEPLOYING and is never issued twice. deploy_sha returns the id string.

When the Society context cannot show a repository read whole within its text budget it cuts the JSON mid-content and still claims nothing was truncated. Cut a read's text (or diff) at whole lines within the same budget, mark it truncated, and report how many lines were shown out of the total (counted like READ_REPO_RANGE) plus the next line to continue from. A partial read must never become a whole-file edit: the prompt must tell the Builder to use replacements instead.

The Phase 5 live driver cannot show why a candidate ended where it did. Add a read-only 'candidates[:<limit>]' plan step that prints each recent candidate's status together with its error, changed files, diff stat, branch, risk tier and QA/Security verdicts and failures, with model-authored text scrubbed and bounded, and teach the plan grammar to accept it with an optional limit.

Every wake the Society Builder has is a one-shot event, so one lost event strands a candidate in REQUESTED forever. Give every open candidate state a role that is woken periodically: the Builder must subscribe to the society heartbeat so the heartbeat reaches it through the dispatch table.

The intent payload schema shown to the model drops every scalar bound, so well-formed work is silently denied (e.g. a 128-character cap on evidence.signal). Render the bounds the typed parser enforces, e.g. 'string(1..128 chars)' and 'integer(0..100)', including gt/lt alongside ge/le, document nested payload models, and state in the prompt that the bounds are hard and not retried.

A JSON-mode model sends an empty string for optional non-text intent fields (e.g. source_task_id), and typed validation rejects the whole intent. In the strict intent payload base, read '' as None for an Optional field whose type is not text (uuid, int, enum, nested model, list); coerce nothing else, keep optional text as given, and record the normalised payload as valid.

Live intents were rejected as invalid and the driver showed only decisions. Add an 'intents:<correlation-id>' driver step that prints per intent its type, risk, policy, execution, the trusted policy or validation reason and executor error (scrubbed, bounded) and only the payload's key names, never values; and make the prompt's schema doc render Optional fields as '<type>|null' and uuid references as 'uuid'.

Maintenance builder: the harness tests an untested worktree at submit / turn limit Live bench x3: a refused-at-final-turn submit lost a correct worktree (tests_not_run), and the green-at-turn-limit submit never fired because the model rarely re-ran tests after its last patch. Now a submit (or a try that ran out of turns) whose current worktree no full test run has judged runs every acceptance test once, without a model call: green is accepted / submitted, red is refused with failing ids, reasons and tail. A worktree already judged is never re-run. # Conflicts: #	services/registry/app/maintenance/config.py Maintenance builder: keep 3 reads per try (live bench: 12 spent the turns reading) Bench x3 on staging, same model: this context with 12 reads gave pass@1 0.361 (15/36 turn_budget); with 3 reads 0.778, pass@3 0.917.

Society: model credential required only where the model is called (#14) On a split deployment (Railway: registry API and society-worker are separate services) /v1/society/status and /config are served by the registry from its own settings. To tell the truth about the running worker during a live window the registry mirrors the NON-secret live flags; validate_settings no longer demands SOCIETY_MODEL_API_KEY in every live-provider process. - config.py: validate_settings(s, model_caller=False); the https rule stays everywhere, the credential rule applies with model_caller=True. - worker.py: startup_problems() = validate_settings(model_caller=True); main() refuses to start (exit 2) without the credential. - tests/society/test_config_validation.py: API mirror without a key validates with truthful public flags; the worker refuses; http refused everywhere.

Society canary: the synthetic anomaly carries the evidence a real one does (#18) Gate A run 12 (Railway staging, real DeepSeek runs): A1 PASS; A2 FAIL with "1 completed run(s), scenario needs 2". The live Scout completed its run, wrote memory and declined to propose: "Another untrusted canary metric anomaly ... with no attached failure artifacts, task ids, or logs" That is the Scout obeying its standing rule — a CREATE_IMPROVEMENT raised for a platform signal MUST carry evidence taken from the event. The canary's injected body carried only metric/value/threshold/description/severity, while the TRUSTED producer (telemetry.produce_anomalies) always emits baseline, sample_size, window_seconds and observed_at. The canary was rehearsing a signal no agent can legitimately act on, so the chain never reached a second role.

Society: name the mandatory payload fields, and an operator path to close a stranded candidate (#29) * Driver: close a stranded candidate through the operator API, never through SQL The abandon endpoint merged in #28 can only be exercised from inside the Railway environment -- this session's egress to *.up.railway.app is blocked by policy -- so the validator needs a step for it, or the remedy ships unproven. abandon:<candidate-id> follows the same discipline as refute:<memory-id>, and for the same reason. The driver holds a database connection, so the one thing this step must not do is the thing it could most easily do: setting status='abandoned' in one statement would "work", leave no audit row and release no escrow -- which is exactly the difference between a remedy and a cover-up.

Promotion: a real promotion could reach every gate and still never finish (#31) The first real autonomous promotion (candidate b8cee13c, promotion c6a8a473, PR #30) published a branch, opened a PR through the Society GitHub App, passed required CI, passed QA, needed no security review and was classified GREEN from the base revision. It then stopped, permanently, on two gates that no action could ever clear. Neither is a model failure; both are defects in trusted code. 1. fitness_precheck could never pass for this KIND of change fitness.py returns "pass" only when a metric IMPROVED: if not hard_ok:      fail elif regressions:    fail elif improvements:   pass else:                inconclusive A documentation change moves no latency and no failure rate, so it lands in the last branch by construction.

Phase 7: production security validation (§38) and the Redis auth contract (§39) (#36) * Production validator: the §38 security suite and the §39 Redis auth contract My Phase 7 verdict claimed GREEN while §55 requires "security PASS", and §38's production security validation had never run. Closing that rather than re-asserting the verdict. §38 — nine anonymous probes, production-safe by construction.

Registry public-edge hardening: verified rate-limit identity and bounded metrics (#43) Two pre-existing registry defects, measured on the public edge, blocked the public LIVE verdict. B1: the rate limiter keyed any "Authorization: Bearer <x>" on a digest of the raw header without verifying it. A garbage token per request got a fresh bucket, and a short one also got the 300/min agent tier. That left login and register unbounded. Now only a JWT the registry signed and that has not expired names a bucket, keyed on its subject. Anything unverified falls back to the edge-reported peer address at the default tier, and the agent tier requires a verified agent token. X1: /metrics labels fell back to the literal request path. The edge client-address middleware copies the scope, so the route annotation never reached the metrics middleware.

Maintenance OS: the scheduled browser probe logs in per run Live-activation finding (implementation defect): the scheduled probe posted with a stored MAINTENANCE_INGEST_TOKEN, a user JWT. User JWTs expire after JWT_EXPIRATION (3600 s by default), so the scheduled deep tier would stop ingesting an hour after the owner configured it, and a rejected post still exited 0/1 like a normal run. - browser_probe.py logs in once per run with an event-producer account (MAINTENANCE_INGEST_EMAIL + MAINTENANCE_INGEST_PASSWORD) on the ingest URL's own origin, then posts with that fresh JWT. A stored MAINTENANCE_INGEST_TOKEN is still accepted for one-off manual runs. - A configured ingress that rejects the login or the report exits 3, so the workflow fails as a broken monitor (findings stay exit 1). - The workflow reads the two account secrets instead of the token.

Maintenance OS: live release preview (exact-SHA parity on a non-production environment) Live-activation finding (implementation gap in the approved design): live_providers() always set preview=None, so every live release would refuse. ADR-0010 D12 and docs/MAINTENANCE_RELEASE.md require a preview that runs the exact candidate SHA. - LivePreview passes only when every service the release changes has the candidate SHA as its ACTIVE (newest SUCCESS) deployment in the preview environment (Railway deployment records, not a guess). Then readiness, the monitored public-surface contract, the A2A card, no public /metrics and no wildcard/echoed CORS for a foreign origin must all hold. "pending" while the SHA builds (the release deadline fails it closed); anything else fails closed.
